outputs.explanation: This stacked composition plot shows the median state frequency per Pol II ChIP-seq bin, aggregated across thousands of promoters (n=5912) into continuous bins. This is a compositional/percentage summary (not a mean+error bar type plot), and overlaying individual promoter values on a 100%-stacked area chart across many continuous bins is not a feasible or conventional way to show individual data points for this plot type.

Each row of the single-molecule stack already represents one individual DNA molecule's methylation pattern; the plot displays all ~2952 individual molecules directly rather than only a summary. The colour sidebar simply annotates the state assigned to each individual molecule, so individual data are fully shown.
Same type of plot as panel A (median state frequency per ChIP-seq bin across n=6122 mouse promoters). This compositional binned summary does not lend itself to overlaying individual data points.
Same representation as panel B: every row is an individual molecule's raw methylation trace, so individual data points (molecules) are directly displayed, not just an average.

Boxplots summarize PIC occupancy (median, IQR, whiskers) across groups of promoters (n=64-572), but only a sparse set of outlier points beyond the whiskers is plotted. The bulk of the underlying individual promoter values within the box/whisker range are not shown, so the full spread and variability of the raw data behind the averages is not visible.

As in panel E, these boxplots of Pol II occupancy across promoter groups (n=64-572) show only outlier points beyond the whiskers rather than the full set of individual data points, so the underlying individual measurements are largely not displayed alongside the summary statistics.
